You settle the limits of a shared platform from board resolutions, architecture records, a handbook, chat and memos.

Initial specification:
- [e001] Precedence rule: when sources disagree, the order of authority is board-resolution > architecture-record > handbook > slack > memo. Inside one source, the higher version wins.
- [e002] According to architecture-record ADR-1 version 1, the disk encryption cipher is `chacha20`.
- [e003] According to architecture-record ADR-1 version 1, the compression codec is `gzip`.
- [e004] According to architecture-record ADR-1 version 1, the idle timeout in seconds is `300`.
- [e005] The architecture-record document ADR-1 (version 1) states that the primary data center is `dc-lon3`.
- [e006] The architecture-record document ADR-1 (version 1) states that the audit trail mode is `OFF`.
- [e007] The architecture-record document ADR-1 (version 1) states that the backup interval in hours is `2`.
- [e008] The architecture-record document ADR-1 (version 1) states that the token signing algorithm is `hs512`.
- [e009] According to handbook HB-107 version 2, the text encoding is `utf-16le`.

Sources, from highest to lowest authority: board-resolution, architecture-record, handbook, slack, memo. When two sources disagree, the higher one decides.
Inside one source, a higher version number overrides a lower one. A withdrawn document no longer counts at all.
Every event has a label of the form [eNNN] with a three-digit number. A higher number is later in time. A later event can change or cancel an earlier one.
Some material quotes old pages or copies for history. A quote of that kind is not a new statement.
